summary:
Bullpen fatigue is the signal of the day: every rating from R1 through R4 shows the exact same +14-15pt hot spike over the last 14 days (R1/R2/R3 at 61% n=18, +14.4pts; R4 at 61%, +15.2pts), and all four carry active 3-game winning streaks on that category. When a category runs this hot across the entire model simultaneously, it's not noise — it's a real market inefficiency on bullpen usage/rest that's printing right now. Pair that with hitting, which is similarly scorching across R1-R3 (R2 leads at 67%, +17.3pts; R1 at 61%, +10.3pts; R3 at 61%, +11.5pts), and any game tonight where bullpen fatigue and hitting both point the same direction on a rating is a green light. Starting pitcher is the mirror image — ice cold across the board (R1/R2 at 39%, -13.9pts; R3 and R4 even worse at -14.2 and -16.1pts) despite each rating's SP read riding a 3-game winning streak, which tells you the streak is lagging the underlying cold trend. Fade any play where SP is the lone category driving the pick.

On tonight's board, lean hardest into R2 and R3 — R2 is the unit leader over the last 7 days (4-1, 80%, +3.0u) and still rolling at 71% over 14 days, while R3 has the best 30-day unit mark among the top three (13-8, +5.0u) and a clean 100% strong-play week. R4 is the one to treat carefully: it's 0-2 for -2.0u over the last 14 days on strong plays despite a healthy 30-day number, so don't overweight its picks tonight even though its bullpen_fatigue read is technically the hottest of the group. If MIL, TBR, BOS or LAD show up as today's picks, trust them without question — all four are running 68-70% hit rates on raw volume and crushing it on strong plays (LAD strong 28-7, 80%, +27.0u is the best number on the sheet). Avoid leaning into NYY regardless of what rating likes them; model is 49% straight and -4.0u on strong plays with that team all season, and nothing in the current hot/cold trends suggests that's changing tonight.
